Indices remain compile-time metadata: pass only the declared payload fields. The retained packages cover both booleans, `"ab"`, the empty string, `"λ🌱"`, zero, and `340282366920938463463374607431768211457`. Full packages contain checked inputs and proof-free results; standalone result-only packages expose the same eight result producers without input-constructor metadata. Open or opaque indices, noncanonical spellings, malformed Unicode scalar text, changed index kinds, and omitted or changed reviewed instantiations are rejected. The required [workflow](https://github.com/seanmorris/lean-bridge/actions/workflows/checked-record-value-index-browser.yml) rebuilds ordinary/reviewed full and result-only packages and runs Node, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit page, React, and worker consumers on pushes and pull requests.

edits.previous: The compiler and reviewed contract admit three canonical index kinds: an unbounded `Nat`, `Bool`, and `String`. They are serialized as unsigned decimal, `true`/`false`, and exact Unicode-scalar text respectively; zero, the empty string, and supplementary characters are valid. Lean reduces a closed expression before recording it, so `1 + 2` and `decide (1 < 2)` become `3` and `true`. Open or opaque values are rejected. `Int`, `Char`, fixed-width or platform-width integers, `Fin`, functions, proofs, instances, and other index types require a separately reviewed representation and are not inferred from a host value. The installed package archives below currently exercise closed `Nat` indices; the broader installed rollout remains separately tracked.

Twelve Chromium/Firefox/WebKit page, React production/Strict Mode and worker executions cover 51 lifecycle observations. Full packages check 16176 assertions, 3031 expected rejections, 8088 calls/snapshots and 3031 recoveries per observation, including constructor selection and normalization. Additional nested checked-record acceptance: Two independent author builds reproduce complete component and runtime archives before source-free offline npm installation. Installed JavaScript and strict TypeScript callers replay after physical relocation. Chromium, Firefox and WebKit each execute page, React production/Strict Mode and dedicated-worker consumers, including missing-Wasm recovery, for twelve browser executions and fifty-one lifecycle observations. The full package checks direct and repeated parameters plus Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing record and active variant fields; exact failures preserve caller graphs and later calls recover. Producer, browser-consumer and destructive-checker revisions are independently frozen. Nested checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Packet, Holder and Choice forms through Array, List, Option, Product and Except copy positions. Generic records, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Other host targets require their own installed evidence. These local Linux x64 Node, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit runs do not establish hosted acceptance. Constructor dispatch counts and peak memory are unmeasured. Complete npm component/runtime archives and original report inputs are retained; browser binaries, React framework archives and generated deployments are represented by recorded identities and observations rather than copied. Additional inherited browser acceptance: The browser installed lane authenticates the ordinary full inherited checked-record package selection for node-javascript, node-typescript, browser-javascript, browser-react, browser-worker. The full API checks valid, normalized, invalid parent, invalid child, alias, nested Fin, repeated-constructor and recovery cases before projecting proof-free results. Two independent author builds, source removal, offline installation, relocation and unchanged caller replay are retained where the host permits them. The fixture covers inherited parent subobjects, child checked fields, aliases, nested inheritance, repeated constructor selections and constructor-free results. Ordinary and independently reviewed sources are exercised in full and result-only npm packages. Node JavaScript, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit execute source-free installed packages; browser contexts cover plain pages, React production and StrictMode, and dedicated workers. Complete component/runtime npm archives, installed receipts, reports, controls, TAP streams and browser observations are retained. Browser binaries and generated deployment directories are represented by their recorded identities and observations. The evidence applies to the exact Linux x64 Node and browser versions recorded in this index. Other hosts require independent installed acceptance. The hosted workflow serializes the four route/mode selections and caps Lean, compiler and build parallelism; peak memory and constructor-dispatch counts are not measured. This archive establishes installed npm/browser behavior, not promotion into the public support inventory. Inherited checked-record acceptance covers only the tested acyclic Span → Ticket → Stamped chain, its Ticket alias, repeated direct parameters, nested parent constraints and proof-free Ticket/Stamped results. Value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, generic or recursive inheritance, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks and owned positions remain unreviewed. Additional recursive browser acceptance: The browser installed lane authenticates the ordinary mutual recursive checked-record selection for node-javascript, node-typescript, browser-javascript, browser-react, browser-worker. Original inputs, exact failures, preserved rejected values, recovery and proof-free results are retained; independently reproduced packages are installed without author sources and replayed after relocation where the host permits it. The archive authenticates local Linux x64 Node, strict TypeScript, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit execution; it does not claim hosted-runner acceptance. Acceptance covers the tested finite mutually recursive Envelope and Branch records/variants, transparent aliases, Array and Option copies; host cycles are rejected and traversal is bounded. Callback, owned, asynchronous and retained-identity positions remain separate requirements. Browser binaries, framework archives and generated deployments are represented by recorded identities and observations rather than copied. Constructor dispatch counts and peak memory remain unmeasured. Recursive checked-record acceptance covers the tested Packet self-cycle and Envelope ↔ Step mutual cycle, their aliases, Array/Option wrappers, active branches, Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields in copied parameters, results and fields. It does not establish generic recursive records, other recursive graph shapes, value-carrying receiver-dependent fields, other index kinds, open dependent or zero-payload records, callbacks or owned positions. Additional hosted closed-index acceptance: Hosted GitHub Actions run 39201330491 at 79359306d2e50a5893affe04cafed95d54166b88 rebuilt all four npm/browser selections on Ubuntu 24.04. This full ordinary-source selection reproduces complete component and shared-runtime npm archives from two author roots, removes author sources, installs offline, relocates the installed tree and replays unchanged Node JavaScript and strict TypeScript callers. chromium 151.0.7922.34, firefox 153.0, webkit 26.5 execute page, React production/StrictMode and dedicated-worker consumers for 12 browser executions and 51 lifecycle observations. The full API exercises all eight checked inputs, exact constructor failures, unchanged rejected values, recovery and all eight proof-free indexed results. The archive authenticates the original workflow, job, artifact, TAP, controls, reports, package receipts and exact source identities. Hosted npm/browser value-index acceptance covers only the archived top-level copied checked-record parameter and result sites with closed Bool, String and Nat indices. Full packages cover parameters and results; standalone result-only packages cover results only. Open or opaque indices; Int, Char, fixed-width and platform-width integers, Fin, functions, proofs, instances and other index kinds; checked-record fields, callbacks and owned positions; value-carrying dependent payloads; and zero-payload checked records remain unreviewed here. Other host targets require separate installed evidence. The Ubuntu 24.04 run records exact Node and browser versions but not peak memory or constructor-dispatch counts. Complete component/runtime npm archives and original workflow records are retained; external toolchains remain trusted recorded inputs."

edits.previous: "checked-record": "Pass only payload fields: Interval {lo, hi}, Triple {data} for Sized 3, and Percent {value} for Bounded 0 101. Input constructors validate cross-field predicates or normalize values inside Lean without changing caller input. Results expose payload fields, not proofs. A standalone result-only package works without any checked input. Generic records, other indices and dynamic dependent payloads are not covered. Packet is a proof-free object with digit: bigint for Fin 10 and word: bigint for a checked Nat Subtype. The selected adapter descends through Array, List, Option, Product, Except, enclosing Holder.packet and the active Choice.packet.value field, applies the exact constructor selected for every public site and nested Word field, and leaves the caller's complete rejected graph unchanged. Repeated parameters keep independent constructor choices; later valid calls recover. Copied Array and Option results contain the same nested payload objects without proof fields or input-constructor selection. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call."

Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call."
